item.location: cyclic.tex tab:kstar and shape numerics (p=13, p=23 switches)
item.what_to_check: Compare with empirical counts in Nanda (5 key freqs p=113), McCracken, Chughtai; flag heuristic cells

chk.evidence:
No prior work computes the maximiser of the L_{1/s}-budget coverage max-min at specific p. None reports switch points in s either. Morwani ICLR24 Thm 7 and Li AISTATS25 Thm 4.1 give dense optima (b = nu). McCracken 2505.18266 Cor 4.8 is a sufficiency bound for random frequencies, with no optimum count.

Empirical counts, all verified from the PDFs:
- Nanda et al. (arXiv 2301.05217), Sec 4.1 / Fig 3. A 1-layer transformer at p=113 uses "five key frequencies ... k in {14,35,41,42,52}". W_E has 6 non-negligible frequencies.
- Chughtai et al. (ICML 2023, PMLR 202:6243-6267), App. Table 6. Transformers on C113 have 3, 4, 4, 3 key frequencies across seeds 1-4.
- Chughtai et al., App. Table 5. MLPs with embeddings on C113 have 13, 11, 15, 10. C118, D59 and D61 have about 9-15 reps.
- Zhong et al. (2306.17844), p=59. Model A's top 3 circles (k=17, 3, 44) give 91.4% accuracy. The full count is not tabulated.
- McCracken et al. 2505.18266, Sec 4.3. Nets with embeddings learn "handfuls of frequencies (3-7)". A log fit of count vs n appears in Fig 3, and Fig 4 covers moduli 59-66. One-hot 1-layer MLPs use floor(n/2).

Our p=113 values (7/4/4) sit inside the empirical 3-15 range. But those models are transformers or ReLU MLPs, not L_{2,b} product/power nets, so the numbers are context and not a validation. Chughtai's MLP counts of 10-15 exceed our nu=3 value of 7.

Heuristic flags:
(a) Enumeration is exhaustive only up to K<=8/7/5. The theorem's K upper bound, 9*4^{1/(s-1)} ln p (about 587 at s=3/2, p=59), does not rule out larger supports. So every cell depends on heuristic search above Kmax.
(b) (113, nu=3)=7 lies above the exhaustive range, and the equal-share argmax gives 5 there (appendix.tex line 260).
(c) (59, nu=3): equal-share gives 6 vs 5.

Searches run: WebSearch "number of key frequencies learned modular addition as function of modulus p" and "optimal number of frequencies max-margin modular addition weight decay sparse K* log p". PDFs grepped: Nanda, Chughtai, Zhong, McCracken, Morwani. Notes are in /Users/ruhaanrajadhyaksha/projects/grok/heracles/paper/litcheck/items/r29-kstar-table/CHECK.md

recommended_citations.why: Empirical p=113 count to set beside tab:kstar: five key frequencies {14,35,41,42,52} in a 1-layer transformer (Sec 4.1, Fig 3). Title and authors confirmed on arXiv; the ICLR 2023 venue comes from the sweep.
App. Tables 5/6 give per-seed key-frequency counts on C113: MLP 13/11/15/10, transformer 3/4/4/3. These show the counts depend on architecture and seed.
Trained transformers at p=59 (the same prime as the table): three circles, k=17,3,44, carry 91.4% accuracy. Title and authors confirmed from the arXiv PDF header.

Sec 4.3 / Fig 3-4: embedding nets learn 'handfuls of frequencies (3-7)', with a log fit of count vs n that includes moduli 59-66. This is the empirical backdrop for the table and the log-p growth. The current refs.bib entry has the wrong title and author.

chk.recommended_change:
Three edits to the table and its text:

1. Caption of tab:kstar: "Support enumeration is exhaustive over supports of size K<=8,7,5 at p=59,71,113; larger supports were searched heuristically, so each entry is the best support found, certified only among K<=Kmax. The entry (113, nu=3)=7 lies above the exhaustive range (equal-share argmax gives 5), so read it as a heuristic value."

2. Sentence at line 133: change "Table~\ref{tab:kstar} gives the counts" to "Table~\ref{tab:kstar} gives computed counts".

3. After the "How many features" paragraph, optionally add: "For comparison, trained networks at p=113 use five key frequencies in a one-layer transformer \citep{nanda2023progress}, 3--4 in transformers and 10--15 in embedding MLPs \citep[Tables 5--6]{chughtai2023toy}, and embedding models generally use 3--7 \citep{mccracken2025,zhong2023clock}. These architectures lie outside our model class, so the comparison is qualitative." Do not claim that Nanda's 5 matches the table.

Also fix the mccracken2025 bib entry.
